newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ambassador left Lima reception early.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador left Lima reception early.

text.p: The two top U.S. diplomats in Peru left a reception at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima half an hour before Peruvian rebels seized it, taking hundreds of hostages, the State Department said on Wednesday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said ambassador Dennis Jett and his deputy chief of mission, who was not named, had been at the reception on Tuesday evening. "They left about half an hour before the terrorists took over the compound," he said.
Citing U.S. policy, Burns refused at a routine news briefing to give any information about any official or private Americans who might be among the hostages.

"The United States condemns in the strongest possible way the brutal hostage taking," Burns said. "We call upon the terrorists who are holding these hostages to release them quickly and safely and unharmed."
"There can be no justification for this shameful act of violence and terrorism."
Latest reports from Lima said as many as 490 people could be being held by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement guerrillas who stormed the reception in a bid to win the release of jailed comrades.
